answer: When a whale falls to the seafloor the survey crew tags every bone and logs it in the registry under the fall's own coordinates. A sable bone bought from a dealer fails the registry: at the marble of the tag the bone must match the crew's own dive record, and a bought bone carries no tag at all. Faking a fall means finding a carcass, diving for a week and paying 15,700, and the tide entry in the registry follows the bone, so a second bone claiming the same tag is confiscated.
